title: Sinclaire Johnson: US Road Mile Record of 4:21.66
excerpt: Sinclaire Johnson ran 4:21.66 at the 2025 Kalakaua Merrie Mile, a new American road mile record. What it shows about training with specific pace targets.
body:
At the Kalākaua Merrie Mile in Honolulu on December 13, 2025, Sinclaire Johnson ran 4:21.66, a new American record for the road mile. It took more than two seconds off Kristin Gear's previous record and ranks second on the world all-time road mile list, behind Diribe Welteji's 4:20.98.

The race used a handicap format, with the women's field starting 31 seconds ahead of the men. Josh Hoey won the men's race in 3:55.15.

Records like this come from training with precise pace targets. In your own speed work, set one pace target per session, such as your goal mile or 5K pace, and run your repetitions at that pace instead of as fast as you feel like on the day. Specific targets turn a hard session into purposeful training.

Sources: LetsRun.com; Honolulu Marathon
keyTakeaway: Give each speed session one specific pace target and run to it, rather than running fast by feel.
